themes_detail.label: Commercial Noise Surge
themes_detail.summary: Commercial noise complaints in Park Slope/Carroll Gardens spiked to 24 THIS WEEK—a 149% jump from the 9.6-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—suggesting a new or intensifying source of disruption in the neighborhood.
evidence: 24 commercial noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 9.6 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 5.65)
149% spike represents statistically significant deviation flagged as high severity
Spike is concurrent with residential and street/sidewalk noise increases, suggesting neighborhood-wide noise escalation
reporting_angles: Identify which commercial establishments (bars, restaurants, construction sites, venues) are driving complaints and interview affected residents on 7th Avenue and Prospect Park West corridors
Check DOB permits against timing of complaints—are new construction projects or ALT-CO filings (224 filed in last 90 days) generating the noise?

themes_detail.label: Street/Sidewalk Noise Spike
themes_detail.summary: Street and sidewalk noise complaints surged to 42 THIS WEEK—a 173% increase from the 15.4 weekly average—indicating possible construction, street vending, or outdoor commercial activity intensification.
evidence: 42 street/sidewalk noise complaints THIS WEEK vs. 15.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.62, severity: high)
173% spike coincides with commercial noise surge, suggesting coordinated neighborhood disruption
Pattern mirrors spring seasonal increases but magnitude is statistically anomalous
reporting_angles: Map complaint locations to identify geographic hotspots—are complaints clustered near Prospect Park West, 7th Avenue, or Flatbush Avenue?
Interview Parks Department and NYPD about enforcement actions; cross-reference with permit data for outdoor vending or events

themes_detail.label: Tree Health Emergency
themes_detail.summary: Dead and dying tree complaints shot to 6 THIS WEEK—a 500% spike from the 1.0 weekly average—suggesting either disease outbreak, storm damage, or deferred maintenance across the district's canopy.
evidence: 6 dead/dying tree complaints THIS WEEK vs. 1.0 weekly average (z-score: 4.47, severity: high)
Aligns with recurring CB budget request for tree maintenance—suggests chronic underinvestment now manifesting as crisis
reporting_angles: Contact Parks Department NYC to identify whether complaints cluster around specific streets (e.g., Prospect Park perimeter, residential blocks) and determine if disease or storm-related
Interview arborists and Parks advocates about whether this signals systemic tree health problems in the district; tie to long-standing CB budget requests for park renovations

themes_detail.label: Parking Crisis Accelerating
themes_detail.summary: Illegal parking complaints jumped 56% two weeks ago (426 complaints vs. 272.8 weekly average) and remain elevated, making it the highest-volume 311 complaint type (3,778 over 90 days) and suggesting parking supply/enforcement crisis.
evidence: 426 illegal parking complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 272.8 weekly average (z-score: 7.08, severity: high)
Illegal parking dominates 90-day complaint volume at 3,778 total, dwarfing next-highest category (heat/hot water at 1,366)
Sustained elevation suggests systemic issue rather than one-week anomaly
reporting_angles: Investigate whether recent zoning changes (GSD Waterfront, 46 Nelson Street rezoning in public review) are driving demand for new construction parking, straining existing supply
Interview residents in high-complaint blocks; check NYPD parking enforcement data to see if ticketing has declined, suggesting enforcement gap

themes_detail.label: Drug Activity Spike
themes_detail.summary: Drug activity complaints surged 700% two weeks ago (3 complaints vs. 0.4 weekly average, z-score 3.77), indicating emerging open-air drug market activity or increased resident reporting in specific locations.
evidence: 3 drug activity complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 0.4 weekly average (z-score: 3.77, severity: high)
700% spike is statistically significant and unprecedented in baseline
Concurrent with maintenance/facility complaints surge (14 THIS WEEK vs. 5.4 avg), possibly indicating public space degradation
reporting_angles: Verify with NYPD precinct whether arrests or incidents match 311 spike; identify geographic concentration (park areas, transit nodes, specific blocks)
Connect to recurring CB budget request for park safety enhancements and interview residents about whether visible dealing has increased
